All three work fine for correcting the details, but Version A — editing right there inline on the bookmark itself — feels the most natural to me. I stay looking at the actual bookmark while I fix it, without a box popping over everything. That's my pick. (The modal and drawer were both perfectly usable too, so this is a preference, not a problem.)

Your assumptions mostly match: yes, starting the correction from the "Edit details" control on the bookmark is right, and title and description are exactly the two I most need to fix for recognizability.

One honest note since you asked about the website name: I'd still expect, somewhere down the line, to be able to fix the actual link itself — like if I pasted the wrong address or it changed. Not necessarily in this same quick "correct the details" spot, and not something to solve right now, but I don't want editing the address to fall off the list entirely. For this correction flow as you've framed it, title and description are the right things to edit here.
